title: Bitnob KYC Document Exposure via Misconfigured AWS Bucket
summary: Cybernews researchers discovered a publicly accessible AWS storage bucket belonging to Nigerian crypto exchange Bitnob, exposing over 250,000 KYC documents including government IDs, passports, and driver's licenses.
details: Cybernews researchers discovered on September 11, 2024 a publicly exposed Amazon Web Services (AWS) storage bucket belonging to Bitnob, a Lagos, Nigeria-headquartered cryptocurrency and Bitcoin-focused fintech platform. The bucket contained more than 250,000 Know Your Customer (KYC) documents used for identity verification during customer onboarding, including government-issued IDs, passports, and driver's licenses. Cybernews attributed the exposure to likely human error involving common cloud-storage misconfiguration. Bitnob secured the bucket following disclosure but had not issued a public statement about the incident as of the researchers' reporting.

title: Betty Gaming Fined Over Age-Verification Control Failures
summary: Ontario's gambling regulator fined online casino operator Betty Gaming CA$120,000 after a self-reported defect in its age-verification and player-eligibility controls allowed underage individuals to register, deposit funds, and gamble on its platform.
details: The Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario (AGCO) announced on August 6, 2026 that it had fined Betty Gaming Ltd. CA$120,000 (approximately $88,000 USD) following an investigation into weaknesses in the age-verification and player-eligibility controls on its regulated online casino platform, Betty.ca. The defect, self-reported by the company to regulators in November 2025, allowed 23 underage individuals to successfully create player accounts, with 9 of them going on to deposit funds and place real-money wagers before the flaw was addressed; a further 14 underage users created accounts without wagering. The AGCO found Betty Gaming had breached provisions of the Registrar's Standards for Internet Gaming requiring operators to prevent underage account creation and to validate player eligibility information as complete and accurate before account creation. Unlike most entries in this tracker, this incident involved a compliance failure in the platform's own age-verification logic rather than a data breach exposing stored identity documents.
